intent: Individually authored tasks distinguish calculation, estimation, prediction, proof and conclusions supported by evidence.

transfer.stem: Which account preserves both event orders and the limit of the evidence?
transfer.passage:
From estimates to evidence
We were asked to calculate how much string we needed. The original instruction gave no lengths. A separate exercise supplied two metres and three metres, giving five metres in total. We also had to estimate a distance before checking a map. An estimate was not an exact measurement.
A question asked us to predict which material would stay dry. It did not report a completed test. One test could not prove that every sample was safe. This did not establish that all samples were unsafe either.
Footprints provided evidence of a small animal. A separate fictional picture compared paw-pad impressions with shoe tread. It had no scale or timestamp and did not establish an exact species. We needed to check the data before drawing a conclusion. We tested a theory with a paper model, but the record did not state that the theory had been proved. Our conclusion had to match the results, even if we had hoped for something else.

options.text: Estimate before checking the map; check data before concluding; a single test does not prove every sample safe.
Check the map before the initial estimate; check data before concluding; one test does not prove every sample safe.
Estimate before checking the map; choose the conclusion before checking data; one test does not prove every sample safe.
Estimate before checking the map; check data before concluding; one test proves every sample safe.

answer.display: Estimate before checking the map; check data before concluding; a single test does not prove every sample safe.
